Some rites attach limited effects to marked sites. It cannot resurrect the dead or identify every killer. Missing records, mistaken identity and fraudulent ledgers undermine results. Mortuary courts, plague registries and battlefield custodians preserve its procedures.
entries.name: POWER — Grave Arithmetic

entries.content: ORIGINAL POWER/TECHNOLOGY TRADITION. Hearth Engines convert fuel, heat, pressure, motion or constrained anomalous materials into repeatable mechanical work. They power pumps, lifts, furnaces, alarms and defined defensive mechanisms. They need fuel, trained operators, seals, replacement parts, ventilation, maintenance and waste handling. Heat, pressure, corrosion and wear accumulate; field systems are harder to repair than workshop systems. There is no perpetual motion.
entries.name: POWER — Hearth Engines

entries.content: ORIGINAL POWER/CRAFT TRADITION. Beastcraft uses verified anatomy, chemistry and carefully processed biological materials to make tools, armor, medicines or limited traits. It requires hunting or lawful sourcing, preservation, skilled processing and transport. No arbitrary monster-part powers are granted. Species variation, spoilage, toxicity and ecological pressure matter; profitable harvesting can collapse a population or create dangerous waste.
entries.name: POWER — Beastcraft

entries.content: ORIGINAL POWER TRADITION. Breath Geometry combines breathing, posture and movement to improve timing, balance, recovery and controlled bursts within biological limits. It consumes oxygen and conditioning, and fails under exhaustion, injury, disrupted breathing or poor footing. It does not create energy blasts or limitless strength. Martial schools, rescue crews and labor guilds teach variants adapted to their tasks.
entries.name: POWER — Breath Geometry

entries.content: ORIGINAL POWER TRADITION. Echo Binding uses tuned spaces, instruments and materials to redirect, focus, dampen or encode sound. Strong effects require prepared geometry and risk acoustic feedback. It is not mind control or universal open-air sound control. Irregular surfaces, moving boundaries, competing noise and broken instruments can defeat it. Underground communities, signal corps and tunnel engineers use its principles.
entries.name: POWER — Echo Binding

entries.content: ORIGINAL POWER/ENGINEERING TRADITION. Thread Calculus uses filaments, knots, tension and anchored mechanical systems for restraints, lifting rigs, trip lines, signals and traps. It requires setup, strong anchors and maintenance. Lines are not invisible, unbreakable or infinite. Inspection, cutting tools, heat, slack or anchor removal can defeat a design. Assassins, rescue crews, stage engineers and bridgewrights adapt it differently.
entries.name: POWER — Thread Calculus

entries.content: ORIGINAL POWER/SURVIVAL TRADITION. Miasma Acclimation combines physiological adaptation, protective equipment and limited symbiosis with a specific anomalous vapor. It may reduce exposure or sense one defined miasma type, at the cost of maintenance, metabolic strain and contamination risk. It grants no universal toxin immunity. Different chemistry, ventilation, barriers and exposure duration remain relevant. Tolerance to one bloom does not imply safety around another.
entries.name: POWER — Miasma Acclimation

entries.content: ORIGINAL ORGANIZATION. The Red Loom is a battlefield witch covenant focused on blood temperature, clotting and management of living tissue through prepared rites. Its doctrine treats the body as a temporary treaty between blood, breath and memory. It is not a Teigu institution. Field medicine and battlefield denial require preparation, materials and trained practitioners; it cannot freely control every living body.
entries.name: ORG — The Red Loom

entries.content: ORIGINAL ORGANIZATION. The Black Hush comprises quiet witch houses specializing in silence, sensory misdirection and concealment of small groups. Its methods combine breath discipline, acoustic geometry and prepared hush-wards, not universal invisibility. It performs extraction, counter-surveillance and refugee concealment. Moving crowds, poor geometry, weather and unfamiliar observers can expose its operations.
entries.name: ORG — The Black Hush

entries.content: ORIGINAL ORGANIZATION. The Ashen Veil is a funeral-witch network responsible for dangerous death rites, plague burials and contested remains. It combines mortuary procedure, salt marks and narrow Grave Arithmetic practices. Its work includes corpse identification, quarantine and inheritance testimony. It needs records, trained staff and proper handling; it is neither a universal necromancer order nor a source of unrestricted resurrection.
entries.name: ORG — The Ashen Veil

entries.content: ORIGINAL ORGANIZATION. The Green Thorn Chapter maintains cultivated warning groves and limited plant-signal networks through Rootsong and species knowledge. It monitors forests, mediates boundaries and restores habitats. Signals are local, slow and ambiguous, and depend on living systems that can be damaged by fire, disease or contamination. It cannot command every plant or instantly know distant events.
entries.name: ORG — The Green Thorn Chapter

entries.content: ORIGINAL ORGANIZATION. The Candle Parliament is a coalition of rival ritual schools that convenes when crises threaten their shared legal privileges. It exists to prevent any one school from defining magic for everyone. Its operations include licensing, arbitration and banned-practice hearings. Multiple incompatible traditions coexist under negotiated procedure; agreement is slow, factional and vulnerable to forged evidence or political capture.
entries.name: ORG — The Candle Parliament

entries.content: ORIGINAL ORGANIZATION. The Ninth Lantern investigates alleged hauntings, false miracles and supernatural incidents using survey tools, trained observation, Salt Memory and ritual countermeasures. It values evidence over fear and conducts investigations, containment and public warnings. Its agents are not omniscient; they can lack access, misread traces or be deceived. A frightening claim remains a claim until supported by evidence.
entries.name: ORG — The Ninth Lantern

entries.content: ORIGINAL ORGANIZATION. The White Briar Hospice treats unusual injuries, curse-like conditions and dangerous power exhaustion through medicine and carefully limited restorative rites. Its doctrine separates care from ownership. Treatment has material, staffing and recovery limits; it does not provide universal healing or erase all consequences. It also supports rehabilitation, quarantine and safer power use.
entries.name: ORG — The White Briar Hospice

entries.content: ORIGINAL ORGANIZATION. The Cinder Choir maintains kilns, controlled burns and emergency firebreaks through Hearth Engine engineering, fuel chemistry and limited heat rites. It handles kiln maintenance, wildfire response, industrial safety and ceremonial cremation. It cannot command all fire. Fuel, wind, ventilation, material conditions and heat accumulation govern what its practitioners can safely do.
entries.name: ORG — The Cinder Choir

entries.content: ORIGINAL PLACE SEED, not manga geography. The Seven Mouths is a canyon delta where seven dry ravines converge during rare floods. Stone sluices and flood markers divide the settlement into hydraulic wards. A blocked gate may protect one district while endangering another. Maintenance labor and downstream rights drive conflict; water engineering determines which routes and neighborhoods remain safe during flood pulses.
entries.name: PLACE — The Seven Mouths

entries.content: ORIGINAL PLACE SEED, not manga geography. Saffron Mile is a caravan service town built around shaded courtyards, animal yards and freight repair. Its wealth comes from verified route information, water-credit clearing and repair contracts rather than a royal palace. Counting halls dominate the skyline. A caravan's delay can affect credit, water allotments, animal health and the town's reputation for reliable route data.
entries.name: PLACE — Saffron Mile

entries.content: ORIGINAL PLACE SEED, not manga geography. Salt Choir Basin is a seasonal salt lake surrounded by low white ridges. Wind through narrow cuts produces tonal sounds interpreted differently by local religious groups. Dust storms erase tracks and damage exposed machinery. Pilgrims and mineral traders compete for access, while changing water levels alter salt quality, crossing routes and the reliability of landmarks.
entries.name: PLACE — Salt Choir Basin

entries.content: ORIGINAL PLACE SEED, not manga geography. Urum's Vent Crown is the surface district above a buried aquifer city. Vent towers, condensation screens and maintenance wells shape its skyline. A sealed shaft may be ventilation, a pressure hazard or a protected water intake, not automatically a treasure room. Access depends on water rights, maintenance authority and the risks of disrupting air or groundwater systems.
entries.name: PLACE — Urum's Vent Crown

entries.content: ORIGINAL PLACE SEED, not manga geography. Ashen Compass is a black-glass volcanic settlement using geothermal channels for kilns and mineral processing. Heat routes separate industrial and residential districts. A failed channel can produce steam, contaminate a cistern or interrupt production. Its infrastructure requires inspection, safe ventilation, repair materials and clear authority over hazardous industrial zones.
entries.name: PLACE — Ashen Compass

entries.content: ORIGINAL PLACE SEED, not manga geography. The Last Shade is a caravan stop at the last reliable tree line before a dry crossing. Shade rights are codified in local law because shelter directly affects survival, animal health and travel schedules. A fallen tree can become an economic and political crisis. Water, repairs, rest capacity and route knowledge determine how many caravans it can safely support.
entries.name: PLACE — The Last Shade

entries.content: ORIGINAL PLACE SEED, not manga geography. The Cold Meridian is a high-desert observatory with underground sleeping halls and wind-protected instrument courts. Its star tables guide caravans across featureless regions. Calendar disputes can delay trade and military movement. Precision instruments need maintenance, and observations depend on weather, horizon visibility, trained interpreters and the age of the tables.
entries.name: PLACE — The Cold Meridian

entries.content: ORIGINAL PLACE SEED, not manga geography. Red Silt Locks is a river-margin industrial town controlling irrigation locks. Neighborhoods are stratified by flood height and canal access. An upstream release can change food prices, damage crops or strand boats. Lock operators, downstream farmers, merchants and local authorities have competing incentives, so a gate adjustment can become a political event with traceable consequences.
entries.name: PLACE — Red Silt Locks

entries.content: ORIGINAL PLACE SEED, not manga geography. Bone-Wind Market is a seasonal market where large animal remains accumulate after droughts. Bone, horn and mineralized tissue are traded under provenance rules. Illegal relic hunters operate beside legitimate anatomists; not every skeleton is a Danger Beast. Material quality, species identification, contamination, processing skill and legal ownership affect value.
entries.name: PLACE — Bone-Wind Market

entries.content: ORIGINAL PLACE SEED, not manga geography. Bellfoundry Below is a cavern industrial settlement where resonance plates relay warnings through tunnels. Mining and construction change acoustic paths, so old signals can become misleading. Production depends on ventilation, transport lifts, support structures and sound calibration. A mine expansion can improve output while breaking warning coverage or creating new hazards.
entries.name: PLACE — Bellfoundry Below

entries.content: CANON STATUS: manga-associated historical anchor; detailed workshop history and individual claims require manga-panel verification. The Empire's founding ruler is associated with commissioning 48 original Teigu as a safeguard for the Empire's future. The catalogue is closed. Unknown registry slots remain unknown, and no character can manufacture, summon or acquire a Teigu by declaration. Keep each item's provenance, demonstrated capability, wielder, status and timeline availability separate.
entries.name: CANON — First Emperor and the 48 Teigu
entries.comment: CANON — First Emperor and the 48 Teigu

entries.content: CANON STATUS: broad historical anchor; exact details require direct manga sourcing. A major civil war centuries before the main story is associated with the loss or disappearance of many Teigu. A registry entry's historical existence does not prove that it survives, is located, is unclaimed or can be acquired in the active campaign. Distinguish manga-shown status, secondary report, original campaign state and unknown.
entries.name: CANON — Imperial civil war and lost Teigu
entries.comment: CANON — Imperial civil war and lost Teigu

entries.content: CANON STATUS: terminology is manga-associated; historical details are partly secondary-source reported and require verification. Shingu is a separate artifact tradition associated in secondary accounts with a later Emperor's attempt, roughly four centuries before the main story, to surpass Teigu. Similar purpose does not make Shingu interchangeable with Teigu. Keep separate registries, manufacturing assumptions, limitations and source confidence; do not merge their power scales.
entries.name: CANON — Shingu is not Teigu

entries.content: CANON STATUS: manga-associated regional tradition; production details require verification. Meihou is a distinct Wakoku-associated artifact tradition. Secondary sources describe it as more reproducible than Teigu when materials and money are available, but that claim must not be generalized into effortless mass production. Keep individual examples and mechanisms source-tagged; original equipment inspired by Meihou must be labeled original, not canon.
entries.name: CANON — Meihou and Wakoku

entries.content: CANON STATUS: manga continuity anchor. The current young Emperor is manipulated by Honest, who is associated with murdering the Emperor's parents. Do not invent securely established names or reign dates for intervening rulers when the manga does not establish them. Original rulers may bridge gaps only when explicitly labeled as RPG expansion and arranged so they do not overwrite manga events.
entries.name: CANON — Emperor, Honest and the current regime
entries.comment: CANON — Emperor, Honest and the current regime

entries.content: ORIGINAL PEOPLES DOSSIER, not manga canon. “Ilyr” is a trade-language umbrella label for long-lived peoples, not one elf kingdom or a uniform culture. The Elarin Watersheds are forest and river communities organized around springs and canopy corridors; the Veyl Steps are highland communities with terraced agriculture and weather observatories; the Nhal Tunnels are subterranean communities shaped by airflow, sound and controlled lighting. Longevity does not imply perfect memory, wisdom, moral superiority or political unity. Their institutions and relationships with the Empire vary by place and period.
entries.name: WORLD — Ilyr communities are not one kingdom
entries.comment: WORLD — Ilyr communities are not one kingdom

entries.content: TAXONOMY CONTRACT. Danger Beast is a specific setting category, not a synonym for every strange organism. Distinguish ordinary fauna, Danger Beasts, sapient peoples, spirits, constructed entities, anomalous organisms, extradimensional entities and environmental phenomena. Appearance alone does not establish intelligence, morality, powers or biology. Recurring types need stable IDs, habitat, physiology, behavior, ecological dependencies, capabilities, limits, resource value and source status.
entries.name: WORLD — Ordinary fauna, Danger Beasts and anomalies
entries.comment: WORLD — Ordinary fauna, Danger Beasts and anomalies
